options: Move dinner to the windowless central room
Stay in the glass room to watch the sky
Open the conservatory roof to vent the pressure
Set up a video camera right outside the window
payload.explanation: A windowless central room is the recommended shelter against flying debris.

payload.snippet: A storm surge from the approaching cyclone is expected to push sea water several streets inland tonight and the local council has urged residents to lift everything off the floor.
options: Lift electronics and important papers onto top shelves
Leave everything on the floor as a test
Tape the front door to keep the surge out
Open the back gate to let the water flow through
payload.explanation: Raising belongings protects against the surge's deepest expected push inland.

payload.snippet: A long drought has weakened the roots of the old oak tree behind the house and the latest forecast warns of a powerful overnight wind storm with sustained gusts of over a hundred kilometres an hour.
options: Sleep in the front bedroom away from the oak side
Sleep directly under the oak to enjoy the breeze
Tie the tree to the roof with a rope
Open every window facing the oak side
payload.explanation: The front bedroom is safe even if the weakened oak falls in the storm.

payload.snippet: A severe heatwave has buckled several stretches of the train track between the two main stations and the rail company has suspended every service for the entire weekend.
options: Reschedule the trip and book a refund online
Walk along the buckled track instead of waiting
Climb onto a parked train to wait there
Try to fix the buckled rail with a hammer
payload.explanation: Rescheduling avoids both heat danger and the legal risk of walking on tracks.

payload.snippet: A sudden derecho has produced straight-line winds powerful enough to flatten part of the city's tree canopy in less than fifteen minutes during the late afternoon commute.
options: Pull off the road into a sturdy car park
Drive faster on the open highway
Park directly under the tallest road tree
Get out of the car to take live video
payload.explanation: Sturdy car parks shelter vehicles from falling branches and rolling debris.

payload.snippet: A flood that has been rising slowly for three days has now isolated the small island village from the mainland and the regional helicopter team has just radioed an evacuation message.
options: Pack one waterproof bag and head to the helipad
Pack four large suitcases for the flight
Stay home and wave the helicopter away
Climb onto the church roof to wait
payload.explanation: One waterproof bag fits the helicopter while letting the team work fast.

payload.snippet: A long-running wildfire has produced smoke so thick across the valley that the air quality index has stayed in the hazardous range for the third consecutive day this summer.
options: Stay indoors with an air filter running
Open every window for fresh air
Go on a long bike ride through the smoke
Run a leaf blower outside to clear the smoke
payload.explanation: Indoor air + a filter cuts smoke exposure far below the hazardous outdoor level.

payload.snippet: A nor'easter has produced enormous waves on the small coastal harbour and the marine forecast has issued a small-craft advisory that lasts well into next Monday morning.
options: Keep all boats moored in the harbour
Sail straight out to ride the biggest wave
Tow the boats out one by one for fun
Anchor in the deepest open water
payload.explanation: Moored boats inside the harbour are the safer choice until the advisory clears.

payload.snippet: A rescue dog adopted three months ago still trembles every time the family vacuum is switched on and now reacts to the sight of any cylindrical appliance during housework.
options: Pair the appliances with high-value treats while keeping them off then gradually power on at distance
Run the vacuum right next to the dog daily until the fear fades
Bin the vacuum and never clean the floors again
Lock the dog in a closet during all cleaning sessions
payload.explanation: Counter-conditioning + distance is the evidence-based way to fade noise + sight fears in rescue dogs.

payload.snippet: The senior family cat has lost weight steadily over the past six weeks and is drinking far more water than usual at every visit to the bowl.
options: Book a vet visit for blood tests covering thyroid and kidney
Switch food brands ten times in a row to see what sticks
Cut the water bowl in half to slow the drinking
Wait three more months to see how it goes
payload.explanation: Increased thirst + weight loss in older cats often signals kidney or thyroid issues that need vet bloodwork.

payload.snippet: The family is moving to a high-rise apartment and the medium-sized dog has lived in a house with a private garden for its entire life so far.
options: Plan multiple daily walks plus an enclosed dog-park visit
Tie the dog to the balcony so it gets fresh air
Lock the dog in the bathroom while you adjust to the new place
Drop the dog at a shelter for the move
payload.explanation: Active medium dogs adapt to apartment life with structured walks + safe off-leash time at dog parks.

payload.snippet: The new pet rabbit has started binkying around the living room in the evenings and the family wants to make the space safer for its zoomies.
options: Cover cables and close off small gaps and remove toxic plants
Let it roam freely with no preparation
Lock it in a tiny cage during all play
Spray cleaning products to keep it away from cables
payload.explanation: Bunny-proofing a space means cable protection + plant safety + closing escape routes.

payload.snippet: The dog has been attending the same daycare for months but the staff have reported new growling at certain visiting dogs in the play yard this week.
options: Pull the dog out and re-introduce slowly with a trainer
Insist the staff make every dog play together
Punish the dog at home for things that happened at daycare
Drop the dog at the busiest daycare in town
payload.explanation: New growling can mean fatigue or pain — a trainer + slow re-intro is the safe path.

payload.snippet: A pet bird has started self-plucking feathers near the chest and the family has tried diet changes already with no improvement after two weeks.
options: See an avian vet for environmental and medical workup
Spray the bird with bitter apple
Tape over the bare patches
Move it next to a louder cage
payload.explanation: Self-plucking has medical + environmental causes that only an avian vet can untangle properly.

payload.snippet: The dog walker has reported that the dog is suddenly leash-reactive to a particular black-and-white border collie that joins their group on Tuesday and Thursday walks.
options: Split the dogs into separate groups and work with a trainer
Force the two dogs together until they sort it out
Skip walks on those days forever
Punish the dog every time it growls
payload.explanation: Splitting + a trainer plan rebuilds polite group walks far faster than forcing contact.

payload.snippet: The family cat has been catching small lizards in the garden every evening and bringing them into the house alive at the back door for the past week.
options: Attach a bell collar and restrict garden access at dusk
Encourage the cat to bring more in
Punish the cat for hunting
Free every lizard outdoors and forget it
payload.explanation: Bells + restricted dusk access reduce the natural cat-hunt drive without punishing instinct.

payload.snippet: The young dog has growled at a child who reached for its food bowl during dinner time at a family gathering last weekend.
options: Manage with a quiet eating space and reward-based training
Take the bowl away every meal as a test
Let the children pet the dog while it eats
Hit the dog whenever it growls
payload.explanation: A protected eating space + reward training is the safe + ethical fix for food guarding.

payload.snippet: A pet hamster's water bottle has been leaking slowly for the past week and soaking one corner of the bedding before being noticed at the weekend cage clean.
options: Replace the bottle and clean and dry the cage fully
Just refill the bottle without checking the seal
Move the hamster to a smaller container forever
Throw out the bedding and skip the new one
payload.explanation: A new bottle + thorough drying prevents mould + respiratory illness in small pets.

payload.snippet: The cat has developed a routine of sitting at the window at five every afternoon waiting for a neighbour's cat that no longer comes to that garden.
options: Offer enrichment toys plus a new view at that time
Take the cat to the neighbour's old garden
Close all the curtains forever
Punish the cat for sitting still
payload.explanation: Enrichment + a new view replaces a routine that no longer offers what the cat wants.

payload.snippet: The puppy has slipped its harness twice on the morning walk this week and bolted across the road toward a tempting park on the other side.
options: Switch to a properly fitted Y-harness plus a backup leash
Skip walks until it learns
Walk on the busy main road instead
Let it off-leash to chase the park instinct
payload.explanation: A fitted Y-harness + backup leash makes bolts physically impossible while training continues.

payload.snippet: The senior dog has started having toilet accidents at night despite being toilet-trained for over a decade with no issues until now.
options: Vet visit plus a midnight toilet break for now
Punish the dog every morning
Stop the dog drinking water from teatime
Lock the dog out in the garden overnight
payload.explanation: Vet checks rule out medical causes while a midnight break helps an older dog manage.

payload.snippet: The new puppy has been crate-trained well but cries for the first ten minutes every time it is left alone, and the neighbours have started to complain about the noise.
options: Build a longer goodbye routine plus a frozen treat
Skip the crate forever
Add a louder TV nearby
Soundproof the entire flat
payload.explanation: A relaxed routine + frozen long-lasting treat shortens the upset window for crate-trained pups.

payload.snippet: A family bird has lost interest in its favourite toys and the family has just upgraded to a bigger cage for it in the lounge.
options: Add foraging puzzles and rotate toys every few days
Take all toys out and start over
Place the cage in a dark room
Force the bird to use the old toys
payload.explanation: Foraging puzzles + rotation keep parrot-family birds mentally engaged in their new larger spaces.

payload.snippet: The dog has been left at boarding for a week and has come home thinner and more anxious than before despite the boarder being trusted by the family.
options: Switch to a different boarding option next time and check the dog over
Use the same boarder again immediately
Stop holidays forever
Punish the dog for losing weight
payload.explanation: Trusted dogs sometimes mismatch a boarder's style — switching protects future trips.

payload.snippet: The kitten has discovered the curtain rail and now jumps onto it from the bookshelf every evening, threatening to pull the whole rail down with its weight.
options: Remove the access point and add a tall climbing tree
Cut the curtains down
Let it keep jumping until the rail falls
Punish it physically each evening
payload.explanation: Climbing trees offer the height a kitten craves without risk to the curtains or the cat.

payload.snippet: The dog has been showing a sore back leg for a few days now after a long off-leash run through rough wooded trails last weekend with another excited dog.
options: Restrict exercise and book a vet visit for a sprain check
Run it hard to work it out
Skip the vet to save money
Tape the leg with packing tape
payload.explanation: Rest + vet check rules out a sprain or soft-tissue injury that can worsen with rough exercise.

payload.snippet: A senior cat has been blocking the litter tray entrance for the other cat in the home and has now started toileting in the laundry basket instead.
options: Provide multiple trays in different rooms
Take both cats out of the home
Move the laundry basket forever
Force the senior cat out of the room
payload.explanation: Multiple trays in spread-out spots ease tension in multi-cat households gently.

payload.snippet: The family pet rabbit has been digging a hole in the corner of its enclosure for two weeks now and the digging has revealed the wire mesh underneath the bedding.
options: Add a dig box of safe substrate to redirect
Flatten the digging area daily
Cover the mesh with thin cardboard
Stop bedding the enclosure
payload.explanation: A safe dig box satisfies a rabbit's natural digging instinct without damage to the enclosure.

payload.snippet: Your school has received a hoax bomb threat by email and the principal has activated the full evacuation protocol covering all six year groups in under five minutes.
options: Follow the marshal's instructions and reach the muster point fast
Stop to collect your school books on the way
Run alone to a different exit you prefer
Stay in the classroom to finish your essay
payload.explanation: Marshals + muster points are designed to account for every student in a real emergency.

payload.snippet: A long-running cyber attack on the school information system has leaked some students' personal contact details on a public forum overnight.
options: Tell a trusted teacher and the school's safeguarding lead immediately
Try to remove the information yourself online
Share the leak link with the whole year group
Ignore it because it isn't your own data
payload.explanation: Safeguarding leads + IT staff are trained to handle leaked student data correctly.

payload.snippet: During the inter-school robotics competition your team's robot has just malfunctioned spectacularly in front of the audience and the judges.
options: Apologise to the judges and explain the recovery plan
Blame a team-mate publicly on stage
Walk off the stage in tears immediately
Quietly switch the robot for another team's
payload.explanation: Calm explanations + a recovery plan turn malfunctions into a respect-winning moment.

payload.snippet: The history teacher has been off ill for three weeks and the substitute is significantly behind on the GCSE syllabus.
options: Form a small study group with classmates and the head of history
Refuse to study because the syllabus is unfair
Memorise old past papers without context
Complain endlessly without proposing anything
payload.explanation: Study groups + head-of-department contact recover lost ground before exam season.

payload.snippet: Your group's coursework has been graded much lower than expected and the marking criteria seems to be applied inconsistently across the year.
options: Request a moderation meeting with the head of department politely
Storm into the staffroom to demand a re-mark
Post the grades on social media to shame the teacher
Submit a complaint to the regulator without checking
payload.explanation: Moderation meetings are the correct channel for marking inconsistencies.

payload.snippet: A student in your year has just disclosed to you that they are being bullied online by an anonymous account on the class group chat.
options: Encourage them to talk to safeguarding and offer to come along
Confront the anonymous account yourself online
Tell other classmates about it for advice
Promise to keep it secret forever
payload.explanation: Safeguarding has the training + tools to handle online bullying disclosures safely.

payload.snippet: Your school's annual exchange trip has been cancelled at the last minute because of a major storm warning in the host country.
options: Help the teacher contact families and reschedule plans
Demand the trip continues despite the warning
Refuse to engage with the new plan at all
Spread rumours about the real reason
payload.explanation: Helping with comms + new plans keeps the year cohort calm during a cancellation.

payload.snippet: The school's sports captain election is going to a recount because of allegations of vote tampering in one of the year groups.
options: Cooperate fully with the recount and accept the result
Demand only your candidate's votes are recounted
Pressure friends to revote in your favour
Boycott the entire process forever
payload.explanation: Cooperation with the recount protects democratic trust at the school.

payload.snippet: A senior teacher you've trusted for years has been publicly accused of professional misconduct and the local press is parked outside the school gate.
options: Avoid talking to press and let the safeguarding team handle the response
Speak directly to the press without any guidance
Spread your own theories on social media
Refuse to attend school until it is resolved
payload.explanation: Safeguarding teams + official statements protect everyone during an investigation.

payload.snippet: Your class has discovered that the practice exam paper they all worked through last week was actually the real exam paper leaked by a leaver.
options: Tell the head of year so the exam can be rewritten
Use the answers and stay quiet about it
Quietly tell only your closest friends
Pretend you never saw the paper
payload.explanation: Telling the head protects exam integrity for everyone in the cohort.

payload.snippet: During a maths exam your calculator stops working unexpectedly twenty minutes into a ninety-minute paper.
options: Raise your hand calmly and request a replacement
Continue trying without saying anything
Stand up and walk out of the exam
Borrow a friend's calculator silently
payload.explanation: Invigilators carry replacement calculators for exactly this situation.

payload.snippet: A school whistle-blower email reveals that some sports team trials are being decided by friendship rather than merit during selection.
options: Submit a formal note via the head of sport requesting transparent trials
Confront the coach publicly during practice
Quit the team in protest without explanation
Spread the email widely on social media
payload.explanation: Formal notes through proper channels are how trials become transparent.

payload.snippet: Your school has been chosen for a high-profile national debate final and you've been picked as one of the lead speakers under intense time pressure.
options: Practice with a teacher and stick to a clear timing plan
Wing the entire speech without preparation
Refuse to participate because of the pressure
Memorise the script word-for-word with no flexibility
payload.explanation: Practice + timing plans handle high-pressure speaking far better than memorising.

payload.snippet: Your school's IT system has been infected by ransomware and all coursework on the network has been encrypted just before the deadline.
options: Backup your own work locally and inform the IT team
Pay any random demand from your own pocket
Open every suspicious email to investigate
Try to crack the encryption with online tools
payload.explanation: Local backups + IT involvement is the standard ransomware response in schools.

payload.snippet: During the long lockdown drill the teacher is signalling silence but a younger student near you has started crying loudly with anxiety.
options: Sit close to them and whisper calmly that they're safe
Walk them across the room loudly to a corner
Tell them off for breaking silence
Run out of the room to find a parent
payload.explanation: Calm reassurance from a peer often steadies a panicked younger student during a drill.

payload.snippet: A serious flu outbreak has hit your year group and the school has asked anyone with even mild symptoms to stay home for the rest of the week.
options: Stay home and complete the work remotely if symptoms appear
Come in to avoid missing the test schedule
Spread rumours about exact case numbers
Demand the school close completely for everyone
payload.explanation: Staying home + remote work slows the outbreak and protects vulnerable classmates.

payload.snippet: Your school is offering a paid summer internship and the application deadline is at midnight tonight after a long day of exams.
options: Submit the application carefully before midnight
Submit a rushed application with typos
Skip the deadline because of exam tiredness
Submit applications for all your friends too
payload.explanation: Submitting a careful application meets the deadline without sacrificing quality.

payload.snippet: During the year-thirteen leaving prom an anonymous social media post has accused one classmate of something untrue and the post is gaining traction fast.
options: Encourage everyone to ignore + report the post
Comment + amplify the post yourself
Confront the accused in person on the dance floor
Take down the dance floor music in protest
payload.explanation: Reporting + ignoring stops harmful viral posts from spreading.

payload.snippet: The school sixth-form careers fair has limited tickets for the most popular workshops and your year is being asked to choose only two.
options: Choose the two workshops that align with your career interests
Choose the most popular workshops just to fit in
Trade tickets on the underground market
Refuse to attend any workshop
payload.explanation: Aligning choices with real career interests turns the fair into useful advice.

payload.snippet: Your school newspaper has been asked to cover a sensitive student welfare story and you've been assigned as the lead student reporter.
options: Work with the head and safeguarding to write a careful story
Publish a sensational version to win readers
Use real names without any permission
Refuse to cover the story altogether
payload.explanation: Careful welfare-led journalism reports the story responsibly + protects students named.

payload.snippet: You're catering a small charity dinner and one of the guests has just disclosed a severe shellfish allergy literally five minutes before the prawn-stock risotto is meant to come out of the kitchen.
options: Plate them a separate vegetable-stock pasta dish + ensure clean utensils
Serve the shellfish risotto and tell them to pick the prawns out
Switch the entire dinner menu in five minutes
Refuse to cater for them at all
payload.explanation: A separate dish + clean utensils is the only safe response to a severe shellfish allergy disclosure.

payload.snippet: Your home-canned tomato sauce has bulged the lid significantly on one of the jars stored at the back of the pantry shelf since last summer's batch.
options: Discard the jar without opening it indoors
Open the jar to smell the contents
Pour the contents over fresh pasta
Re-process the jar in a hot water bath
payload.explanation: Bulged home-canned lids signal botulism risk — discarding unopened is the only safe response.

payload.snippet: Your commercial kitchen has just lost gas pressure during the dinner-rush hour and twenty plated mains are stalled on the pass right at the busiest time.
options: Switch to electric induction stations + plate cold-prep first
Wait for gas to be restored before sending anything
Light candles for makeshift flames
Comp the entire room and close the kitchen
payload.explanation: Induction back-up + cold-prep first keeps service moving through a gas outage.

payload.snippet: Your sourdough starter has been refused a transit visa at the airport security and you've discovered fermented food restrictions only at the gate during international travel.
options: Plan to dehydrate the starter for travel next time
Try to smuggle the starter onto the plane
Discard the starter at the airport bin
Ship the starter dry via separate post
payload.explanation: Dehydrated starter passes most customs + can be rehydrated at the destination.

payload.snippet: A senior food-safety inspector has arrived unannounced at the catering kitchen halfway through a high-volume wedding banquet preparation.
options: Pause prep to walk the inspector through every station calmly
Hide the temperature logs immediately
Continue prep at full speed and ignore the inspector
Try to bribe the inspector with a meal
payload.explanation: A calm walk-through with logs handy is the correct response to an unannounced inspection.

payload.snippet: Your kitchen freezer has been at minus two degrees for over thirty hours during the recent ice storm and the freezer alarm has just gone off.
options: Discard frozen meat and seafood + assess remaining items
Refreeze everything immediately when power returns
Continue using everything as normal
Take a photo for the insurance and freeze it all back
payload.explanation: Above minus six degrees for that long puts frozen proteins outside the safe zone.

payload.snippet: Your large-batch curry has just been declared too spicy by the head chef for the venue and the service window opens in fifteen minutes for two hundred plates.
options: Stir in cooled yogurt + coconut milk to balance heat
Add ten times more sugar to the pot
Strain out every chilli piece manually
Send the curry as is and hope for the best
payload.explanation: Dairy + coconut milk neutralise capsaicin much faster than sugar or straining.

payload.snippet: Your vacuum-packed sous-vide bag has just split open inside the water bath during a four-hour cook of a delicate piece of fish.
options: Discard the fish for food-safety reasons
Re-bag and continue cooking
Eat it raw to save time
Boil the broken bag in the same water
payload.explanation: Bath-water contamination during a long cook makes the fish unsafe to serve.

payload.snippet: Your restaurant team has been told a noisy plumbing repair will be happening in the building next door during the entire Saturday lunch service this weekend.
options: Plan a quiet-cook menu + warn diners before service
Open as normal and absorb the noise
Move tables outside without licensing
Refuse to open at all that day
payload.explanation: Quiet menus + diner warnings keep the kitchen viable through a noisy neighbour.

payload.snippet: Your home oven has just failed silently in the middle of baking a wedding cake order for tomorrow morning.
options: Borrow a neighbour's oven + finish the bake
Continue baking in a cold oven
Microwave the cake to finish it
Cancel the wedding cake last minute
payload.explanation: Neighbours' ovens or a community kitchen often rescues a baking emergency.

payload.snippet: Your seafood supplier has just delivered a batch of clams that don't close when tapped firmly on the work surface during the final pre-service quality check.
options: Discard the open clams that won't close
Cook them anyway in the chowder
Force the shells closed with rubber bands
Soak them in cold water and try again
payload.explanation: Open clams that don't close when tapped are dead — they aren't safe for service.

payload.snippet: Your kitchen team has just suffered a knife injury during an extremely busy weekend brunch service with a queue at the door.
options: Send the injured cook to first aid + reshuffle stations
Carry on with the injured cook on the line
Close the kitchen entirely mid-service
Apply a bandage and continue cutting
payload.explanation: First aid + a station reshuffle keeps people safe + service moving.

payload.snippet: Your charity bake sale has discovered that one of the volunteers has been using a recipe that contains alcohol after the rule against alcohol was made very clear last week.
options: Remove the affected items + label everything else clearly
Sell them anyway since they're already baked
Reheat to evaporate the alcohol off
Quietly skip the rule next time
payload.explanation: Removing + clear labelling protects buyers who chose the sale because of the rule.

payload.snippet: Your kitchen waste-water grease trap has overflowed during the dinner-rush + the smell is starting to reach the dining room.
options: Stop service briefly + call the grease-trap company
Pour bleach down the drain to mask it
Open every window and continue serving
Mop up the grease with paper towels
payload.explanation: Stopping service + a specialist call is the only safe + lawful response to a grease overflow.

payload.snippet: Your batch of homemade fermented hot sauce has been infested with fruit flies overnight despite the lid being on tight.
options: Discard the batch + sanitise the area thoroughly
Sieve the flies out + bottle the sauce
Boil the sauce to kill the eggs
Add vodka to mask the contamination
payload.explanation: Fly contamination in fermenting food is one-strike — discarding + sanitising is the safe call.

payload.snippet: Your friend has just discovered a tooth filling in the dish you cooked at last night's potluck dinner during the post-dinner clean-up.
options: Apologise sincerely + cover the dental costs
Deny the filling came from your cooking
Blame the supermarket loudly
Avoid speaking to the friend ever again
payload.explanation: Owning the mistake + covering costs is the only path through a serious food incident with a friend.

payload.snippet: Your high-altitude bake has produced collapsed soufflés despite following the standard recipe to the letter at the new mountain location.
options: Adjust the leavening + protein ratios for altitude
Bake at home altitude only forever
Add ten extra eggs to compensate
Bake at twice the temperature
payload.explanation: High-altitude baking needs proven altitude-specific tweaks — not bigger doses of standard ingredients.

payload.snippet: Your child has just announced a class allergy alert for the whole class includes a brand-new ingredient and the bake sale starts tomorrow morning.
options: Rebake everything with safe substitutes overnight
Skip the alert and bring as planned
Refuse to participate in the sale
Bring food labelled 'may contain' loosely
payload.explanation: Overnight rebake with safe substitutes is the only ethical move for a class-wide allergy alert.

payload.snippet: Your kitchen has just been informed that a recall has been issued on the brand of flour you've been using for the bakery's entire run this week.
options: Discard affected products + contact recent customers
Continue selling the existing bakery items
Use the flour only on internal staff meals
Hide the recall from the team
payload.explanation: Recalls require pulling product + reaching the customers who already bought to protect them.

payload.snippet: Your community kitchen is hosting a fasting community's after-fast meal and the timing must be exact within five minutes of sunset for cultural reasons.
options: Plan a hot-hold + final-touch service for sunset
Serve early to be on the safe side
Serve late and apologise
Skip the planning and improvise
payload.explanation: Hot-hold + final-touch service hits the exact sunset window respectfully + safely.
